samples.question: Exactly one square plate in this picture is drawn with a black border; every other plate is drawn with a pale lavender border. The black-bordered plate is divided into an 11 by 11 grid of 121 equal square cells, and every cell is filled with one of just two tones, a darker tone and a lighter tone. The three-square key near the bottom left shows those two tones with their exact midpoint tone between them. Nearby, separated from the plate by plain background, are exactly two small black marks: one hollow black ring and one solid black square. They are the gauge. The distance between the centres of the two black marks is a whole number of plate cell widths, either horizontally, or vertically, or the same whole number of cell widths in both directions at once; that whole number is the slide length in cells, and the slide runs in the direction that leads from the hollow ring to the solid square. Carry out this operation. Take a copy of the black-bordered plate's own pattern of darker cells. Slide the whole copy across the plate by the gauge's slide, that many cells in that direction. Lay the slid copy back over the plate and mark every cell of the plate that is darker in the plate and is also covered by a darker cell of the slid copy; any part of the copy pushed off the edge of the plate is discarded. The marked cells form exactly one symbol inside the middle 5 by 5 block of the plate: 'plus' is that block's full centre row together with its full centre column, 'ex' is that block's two full diagonals, 'tee' is that block's full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is that block's full left column together with its full bottom row. The plate on its own shows no symbol, the two black marks carry no pattern of their own, and the lavender plates, the lavender marks and the key are decoration. Which symbol do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, ex, tee, ell.
